fixes.explanation: Look at the verse again, friend. It says, "The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 9:5) That's the Wilderness of Sinai, twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. They did it, start to finish. Me? I once stamped a whole batch upside down and called it a design choice.

The men ask something different. They say, "…why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?" (Numbers 9:7) Their question is about being left out of the offering. Nothing in the verse mentions someone else eating their share.

Close, friend, but that's not their question. They say, "…why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?" (Numbers 9:7) Their words are about the offering and being excluded from it. Leaving the camp isn't in what they ask.

That's what the text says. "…if a man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey still fails to observe the Passover, he must be cut off from his people…" (Numbers 9:13) Notice the two conditions: ceremonially clean and not on a journey. It's a serious line, so I'll just say it plainly. The text says he must be cut off.

The second month is for a different kind of person, friend. Verses 10 and 11 give it to someone unclean because of a dead body or away on a journey. For a man who is ceremonially clean and not on a journey, the text says, "…he must be cut off from his people…" (Numbers 9:13) This one is heavy, so let's take it seriously.
